author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader filters the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty filter and return only the veterinarians holding that specialty. The filter is named in the request; neither surface gains a page control.
acceptance_criteria: Both the veterinarian directory page (/vets.html) and the machine-readable directory (/vets) accept an optional `specialty` query parameter.
Given a specialty two veterinarians hold, either surface returns only those two.
The specialty name matches in full and disregards letter case; the opening letters of a specialty name match no veterinarian.
A specialty no veterinarian holds returns the ordinary page or document with an empty veterinarian list and a success status, not an error.
An empty or all-space specialty value behaves as though the parameter were absent, as an empty owner search does.
A specialty value with leading or trailing spaces returns the same veterinarians as the value without them.
Pagination links on a filtered page carry the specialty, so a later page stays filtered to it.
The page count and item total of a filtered page count the filtered veterinarians, not every veterinarian.
With no specialty parameter present, both surfaces behave exactly as they did before.
Neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other control for choosing a specialty.
non_goals: A visible control — form, dropdown, or link — for choosing a specialty on either surface
Free-text veterinarian search, which NG-9 still declines
Filtering by more than one specialty in one request
Filtering the directory by any attribute other than specialty
Telling the reader that no veterinarian holds the named specialty
notes: REQ-VET-003 (machine-readable directory reinstated as a supported surface) carries no slice of its own: the surface already behaves as required, and this slice's unfiltered-JSON criterion is its regression cover. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its ID is not reused. Three open questions are recorded in the PRD rather than consulted, per the dispatch: several specialties at once, a visible control, and an empty-result message. The narrowest reading was taken on space trimming, following REQ-OWN-002's precedent, which the dispatch cited for the blank case.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed. Free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in scope. Record the narrowing the way this project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice adds one request parameter to an existing feature package and needs no new type, package, or pattern. The vet package already holds the entity, the Spring Data repository, and the controller together (system-design.md#package-structure), and the owner feature already demonstrates a request-parameter narrowing over a paged list. The adjustment is three-fold: two narrowing finders on VetRepository mirroring its existing findAll pair, an optional specialty parameter on both VetController handlers, and pagination links in vetList.html that carry the active filter. Read directly from the working tree, not resolved through the IDE oracle (not connected in this dispatch): VetRepository.java:44-56 holds the cached findAll pair, VetController.java:44-72 holds the two handlers, and OwnerController.java:98-107 holds the strip-and-blank-means-all precedent the blank-value criterion cites.
integration_points: VetController: both /vets.html and /vets take an optional specialty request parameter; absent, empty, or all-space behaves exactly as today, which is the regression cover REQ-VET-003 relies on

VetRepository: two narrowing finders mirroring the existing findAll pair — one collection-returning for the machine-readable surface, one Pageable-taking for the paged page — with the case fold expressed in the query itself (Spring Data IgnoreCase, or an explicit lower() in JPQL as PetTypeRepository does)
vetList.html: the five pagination links carry the active specialty, so page count, item total, and every link stay inside the filtered set
system: the vets cache keeps only the unfiltered finders; the narrowing finders are not annotated Cacheable

patterns.description: strip the parameter and treat a blank value as the broadest result — the precedent the blank-specialty criterion cites; reuse the shape, not the notFound rejection that follows it
derived paged finder over a request-supplied value; the narrowing finders follow this shape rather than a hand-written query
the existing cached findAll pair the two new finders mirror in arity and return type
repository-level vet test against the real schema and seed data; the home for the matching-semantics coverage a mocked controller test cannot carry

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching left to the column type or the vendor collation repeats Known Defect 1, where PostgreSQL owner search is case-sensitive while H2 and MySQL are not. The H2-backed default suite cannot observe the divergence.
risks.mitigation: Express the case fold in the query (IgnoreCase in the derived name, or lower() on both sides in JPQL) so all three vendors fold identically, rather than relying on VARCHAR_IGNORECASE or a default collation.

risks.risk: Annotating the narrowing finders Cacheable would key the vets cache on an unbounded, unauthenticated, caller-supplied string. CacheConfiguration declares that cache with statistics only and no size limit or eviction, and no provider configuration file exists in the tree — a request loop with distinct specialty values grows it without bound. security-principles.md forbids a change that worsens the demonstration baseline.
risks.mitigation: The narrowing finders carry no Cacheable annotation. Recorded as state in system-design.md#contracts and scoped against Open Question 5.

risks.risk: Building the filtered pagination hrefs by string concatenation would emit a request-derived value into a URL unencoded — a value containing a space or an ampersand breaks the link, and the pattern teaches unsafe URL assembly in a sample others copy.
risks.mitigation: Use the Thymeleaf link-expression parameter form, @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=...)}, which URL-encodes each value and omits a null parameter, so the unfiltered page renders links identical to today's.

risks.risk: Paging over a collection join can duplicate rows and inflate the page count.
risks.mitigation: vet_specialties holds each vet-specialty pair once, so the join yields at most one row per vet. The page-count criterion is the assertion that proves it; keep it in the test set.

risks.risk: The owner precedent rejects an empty result with a notFound binding error. Copying it wholesale would breach the criterion that an unheld specialty returns the ordinary page or document with a success status, and the non-goal that forbids telling the reader.
risks.mitigation: The two handlers take no BindingResult and add no message; an empty filtered result renders the ordinary page with an empty list.

risks.risk: VetControllerTests is a WebMvcTest with a mocked VetRepository, so the whole-name, case-insensitive, and prefix-matches-nothing criteria would assert the stub rather than the behavior. Three acceptance criteria would be nominally green and actually unproven.
risks.mitigation: Keep the controller-level names from the prd-entry for wiring, parameter carry-through, and pagination, and add repository-level coverage for the matching semantics alongside ClinicServiceTests.shouldFindVets, against the seeded specialties — surgery is held by two veterinarians, which the two-veterinarian criterion needs.

notes: Durable-memory writes this dispatch: docs/adr/README.md gains the index row for the 2026-08-12 non-goal ADR. docs/system-design.md — the Overview no longer claims there is no JSON API and now names the machine-readable directory; the Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, and VetController contract rows map to REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004, and Vets loses its em-dash so the three-kinds statement above the table is true again; the Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route requirement-less is removed, since REQ-VET-003 supplies one; Security Context lists the specialty-filter parameter as an input; Open Question 5 records that filtered reads stay outside the cache; the provenance blockquote now says post-survey statements come from recorded decisions rather than the tree. No ADR was written — the caching asymmetry is a one-annotation reversible choice, and the product decision behind the slice is already carried by the Accepted 2026-08-12 non-goal ADR, which is product-owned. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit had nothing to judge. The scope_overrides entry on the prd-entry is already honored: the NG-9 narrowing is recorded in that ADR and its index row now exists.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The specialty filter is the slice's one request-derived value reflected back into rendered HTML, and its entire XSS mitigation is structural: the pagination links use the Thymeleaf link-expression parameter form, which URL-encodes the value. Nothing pins that structure. The neighbouring pagination template (src/main/resources/templates/owners/ownersList.html:35-54) builds its links by string concatenation with preprocessing (@{'/owners?page=__${currentPage - 1}__'}), so the unsafe form is the in-repo precedent a future edit is most likely to copy; switching vetList.html to it would silently reintroduce an unencoded reflection with no test failing. The existing assertion covers only a benign value ('/vets.html?page=2&specialty=radiology'), which passes under both the safe and the unsafe form. Class sweep: specialty is the only request-derived value reflected into a link in this change set; the owners pagination links carry no request-derived value, so this is the single instance.
findings.fix: Add one MockMvc case to VetControllerTests alongside theVetListPaginationShouldCarryTheSpecialtyFilter that drives a hostile specialty value (for example "radiology\"><script>alert(1)</script>") through GET /vets.html and asserts the rendered body does not contain the raw "<script>" sequence and does contain the percent-encoded form in the pagination href. That pins the encoding property rather than one benign string.

recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD this pass: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, so no CVE match ran, and this reviewer has no network access. The change set adds no dependency and does not touch build.gradle (Spring Boot stays at 4.1.0), so the slice introduces no new supply-chain exposure — the unverified check is a standing project gap for CI or a human to close, not a finding against this change.

Pre-existing and out of scope for this slice, recorded so it is not lost: /vets.html binds page as a primitive int with no lower bound, so page=0 reaches PageRequest.of(-1, 5) and surfaces as a 500 through the error page, which docs/system-design.md Known Defects already records as rendering the exception message. The new specialty parameter neither causes nor worsens this.
approved_aspects: No injection path: both new finders are Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase), so the caller-supplied name is bound as a JPA parameter; a sweep of src/main/java/.../vet/ for Runtime, ProcessBuilder, exec(, createQuery, @Query, String.format and Jackson polymorphic typing returns nothing

Reflected-output escaping verified rather than assumed: every pagination link in templates/vets/vetList.html:33-60 uses the @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} parameter form, which URL-encodes the value, and the template selects between a filtered and an unfiltered expression so a null filter is dropped instead of rendering empty. No th:utext and no __${...}__ preprocessing anywhere in the new markup, so no request text reaches template-expression evaluation

Cache-poisoning/unbounded-growth mitigation verified at the source: CacheConfiguration.java:49-51 builds the 'vets' cache from a bare MutableConfiguration with statistics only, confirming the javadoc's own note that no size limit or eviction policy is set. Keying that cache on a caller-supplied string would let a request loop grow the heap without bound; both narrowing finders in VetRepository.java correctly omit @Cacheable and carry the reason inline

Input normalisation fails safe: VetController.filterFor collapses null, empty, and all-space values to null, so a blank parameter widens to the unfiltered query instead of matching an empty specialty name; no unbounded allocation is introduced, since the unpaged /vets result set was already the full collection

Security Context and Threat Model in docs/system-design.md both name the new unauthenticated input and state the reflected-link mitigation, so the next reviewer inherits the boundary rather than rediscovering it

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The Veterinarian directory section stacks all three anchors (req-vet-001, req-vet-003, req-vet-004) at the top of the section, but REQ-VET-004 is not first-mentioned until the second paragraph — it belongs to a separate paragraph from REQ-VET-001/REQ-VET-003. Every sibling section (Owner records, Pet records, Visits, Language, Entry point) stacks its anchors only when all tagged IDs are mentioned within one contiguous paragraph; this section breaks that pattern by front-loading an anchor for a requirement not mentioned until a later paragraph. The result: the ADR's separate deep-links to prd.md#req-vet-003 and prd.md#req-vet-004 resolve to the identical scroll position, losing the distinction between the two requirements' first mentions.
findings.fix: The clinic publishes the veterinarians it employs with the specialties each holds, listed a page at a time. A veterinarian holding no specialty is shown as having none rather than left blank `[REQ-VET-001]`. The clinic publishes the same directory a second time in machine-readable form, for readers that consume the list rather than read it `[REQ-VET-003]`. Either form of the directory accepts a specialty filter, leaving only the veterinarians who hold the named specialty `[REQ-VET-004]`. The reader names the specialty in the request; neither form carries a control for picking one. A name matches a specialty in full and disregards letter case, so the opening letters of a specialty match nothing. Naming a specialty no veterinarian holds gives the ordinary directory with no veterinarian in it, rather than a failure. Naming nothing, or only spaces, gives the whole directory, as an empty owner search does. Paging through a filtered directory keeps the filter.

The clinic publishes the same directory a second time in machine-readable form, for readers that consume the list rather than read it `[REQ-VET-003]`. Either form of the directory accepts a specialty filter, leaving only the veterinarians who hold the named specialty `[REQ-VET-004]`. The reader names the specialty in the request; neither form carries a control for picking one. A name matches a specialty in full and disregards letter case, so the opening letters of a specialty match nothing. Naming a specialty no veterinarian holds gives the ordinary directory with no veterinarian in it, rather than a failure. Naming nothing, or only spaces, gives the whole directory, as an empty owner search does. Paging through a filtered directory keeps the filter.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain again not verified against the NVD this pass, for the same standing reason as round 1: no OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured and this reviewer has no network access. The fix delta changes no dependency and does not touch build.gradle, so the slice's supply-chain exposure is unchanged; the unverified check remains a project gap for CI or a human, not a finding against this change.

Still open and still out of scope for this slice, recorded so it survives: /vets.html binds page as a primitive int with no lower bound, so page=0 reaches PageRequest.of(-1, 5) and surfaces as a 500 through the error page. The delta neither causes nor worsens it.
approved_aspects: Round-1 finding (line 17) is resolved. theVetListPaginationShouldEncodeASpecialtyCarryingMarkup (VetControllerTests.java:162-170) drives "radiology\"><script>alert(1)</script>" through GET /vets.html and pins the encoding property rather than a benign string. Verified it discriminates the safe form from the unsafe one by walking both renderings: under the current @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} parameter form Thymeleaf percent-encodes the value, so the body carries specialty=radiology%22%3E%3Cscript%3E and no raw <script>; under the ownersList.html concatenation-with-preprocessing form the value lands in the href raw and is HTML-attribute-escaped to "><script>, which still satisfies the no-raw-<script> assertion but cannot satisfy the percent-encoded assertion. The unsafe form therefore fails the test, which is exactly the regression guard the finding asked for.

The deliberate deviation to a prefix assertion is sound and I would have preferred it. radiology%22%3E%3Cscript%3E already pins the three characters that carry the attribute-breakout (" > <) in percent-encoded form; the omitted tail (alert(1)</script>) contains only characters whose encoding differs between RFC 3986 query-escaping and URLEncoder and adds no discriminating power, since no rendering exists in which the prefix encodes correctly and the tail does not. Pinning the full value would have coupled the test to a Thymeleaf implementation detail without strengthening the security property.

The no-raw-<script> half of the assertion is non-vacuous rather than trivially true: swept src/main/resources/templates/ for the literal <script and confirmed the only occurrence reaching a /vets.html render is layout.html:84 (<script th:src=...>), which does not contain the asserted <script> sequence, so the assertion can genuinely fail if an unescaped tag ever lands in the body.

Class sweep over the full fix delta: the specialty parameter remains the slice's only request-derived value reflected into rendered output, and the delta touches no production code (docs/prd.md anchor split plus two test files), so no new reflection, sink, or trust boundary was introduced. The five ClinicServiceTests renames and theVetSearchShouldReturnAVeterinarianUnderEachSpecialtyItHolds are pure repository-level assertions with no security surface.

The two added /vets JSON cases extend the fail-safe input normalisation to the JSON boundary: theVetResourceShouldReturnEveryVeterinarianWhenTheSpecialtyIsBlank pins that an all-spaces parameter widens to the unfiltered query rather than matching an empty specialty name, which is the same fail-secure behaviour previously verified only for the HTML form.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theVetSearchShouldReturnAVeterinarianUnderEachSpecialtyItHolds asserts found.extracting(Vet::getLastName).contains("Douglas") for the dentistry specialty. Checked the seed data (src/main/resources/db/h2/data.sql): specialty id 3 is dentistry and vet_specialties has exactly one row for it (vet 3, Douglas), so Douglas is the only dentistry holder today. contains() is looser than the data supports and would silently pass if findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase regressed to return extra, unrelated vets alongside Douglas -- a real defect this edge-case test exists to catch. containsExactly is available and equally simple given the known, single-row seed fixture; the checklist (docs/testing-principles.md AssertJ Assertions) prefers exact collection assertions over loose ones. Swept the rest of the fix delta for the same pattern: the sibling test theVetSearchShouldReturnOnlyVetsHoldingTheNamedSpecialty already uses containsExactlyInAnyOrder against the same seed data, and the two new JSON-resource tests use hasSize -- this is the only loose collection assertion in the delta.
findings.fix: Change the assertion to assertThat(found).extracting(Vet::getLastName).containsExactly("Douglas"), matching the precision of the sibling surgery test.
